title: Cards
summary: Cards group a coherent unit of content or action; they are not a default layout primitive.

MUST.text: Use a card only when content has a meaningful boundary or independent scan unit.
If the whole card is clickable, provide one dominant destination and an accessible name; avoid competing nested actions.
Preserve semantic structure (heading, list, etc.) inside the card; do not rely on card chrome alone.

SHOULD.text: Keep nested actions clearly separated and keyboard-focusable; provide hover/focus affordance.
Use consistent spacing and elevation tokens from the design system.

AVOID.text: Do not put every paragraph in a card or use grids without content rationale.
Do not nest multiple competing click targets in one card.

EXAMPLE.good: Project card groups name, status, owner and one Open action
EXAMPLE.bad: every paragraph wrapped in a card in a three-column grid

FAILURE_MODES: Card grids without content rationale create visual noise and scanning cost.
Whole-card clicks with nested actions cause accidental navigation.
Missing semantics make card content hard to navigate for assistive tech.
